headline: COPPER DEFIES SELL-OFF — $14,044 Holds as China Spot Premium Hits 2021 High of 1,900 yuan/t
snippet: LME three-month copper recovered to $14,044.50/t Thursday after touching a 2.5-month low of $13,883 on November 3, as the Shanghai physical spot premium surged to 1,900 yuan/t — the widest since 2021 — signalling robust Chinese smelter restocking demand even as macro-driven futures selling persists. The divergence between weak paper pricing and tight physical supply is a classic early indicator of a demand-led floor in copper.

headline: GLOBAL MINERS SURGE POST-MIDTERM — ASX Materials Up 7%, European Mining Stocks Rally on Dollar Collapse
snippet: Australia's materials sector surged approximately 7% on November 5 as the US dollar's post-midterm drop filtered through to ASX-listed gold, copper and diversified miners, while European-listed mining stocks also rallied sharply as the dollar fell against sterling and the euro. The ASX 200 itself climbed roughly 2% on the day, with resources the standout sector, extending a recovery across global mining equity markets that began when US election results landed overnight.

headline: MAJOR DRILLING EXPANDS TO AUSTRALIA — $50M Bunbury Buy Adds Mine Dewatering Division to Drilling Giant
snippet: Major Drilling Group International acquired Bunbury Drilling Company of Western Australia for $50 million upfront plus up to $20 million in performance earnouts over three years, adding a mine dewatering drilling specialty to its core contract drilling operations. The deal gives Major Drilling an immediate footprint in Australia's active iron ore, gold, and lithium mining regions, where dewatering demand from deep underground and open-pit operations is growing rapidly.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING DOME SCALES UP — 36 Holes Extend High-Grade Gold 600m South; Open-Pit Case Confirmed
snippet: Discovery Mining's 36-hole drill program at the Dome project in Ontario returned high-grade gold intercepts that extend the mineralized zone approximately 600 metres to the south, with management saying the results confirm the case for a much larger open-pit operation than previously modeled. The footprint expansion materially increases the exploration target and sets up a resource estimate revision that could substantially upgrade the project's economic profile.

headline: UR-ENERGY SHIRLEY BASIN MINING — Wyoming ISR Reached Full Operations in August 2026; Q3 Results Incoming
snippet: Ur-Energy (TSX: URE) confirmed its Shirley Basin in-situ recovery mine in Wyoming achieved full operations in August 2026 as the company set its Q3 2026 results date, adding to its flagship Lost Creek ISR project and making it the second-largest uranium producer in the United States. The Shirley Basin ramp-up adds production at a time when US uranium output is under heightened strategic scrutiny ahead of the November 10 China rare earth export control decision.

headline: SPROTT URANIUM TRUST HALTS SPOT BUYING — 12.77% NAV Discount Removes Market's Largest Discretionary Buyer
snippet: The Sprott Physical Uranium Trust (TSX: U.UN) traded at a 12.77% discount to its net asset value on November 4 and suspended its at-the-market spot uranium purchases, temporarily removing what had been the market's largest discretionary physical buyer from the spot market. The halt matters because Sprott's buying programme underpinned significant price support in earlier cycles; with the trust sidelined, the spot market becomes more reliant on utility procurement and financial-buyer demand to maintain the $92/lb floor.

headline: SSR MINING CLOSES ROXMORE DEAL — Nevada Gold Footprint Grows; Converse Project Acquisition Flagged as Next Step
snippet: SSR Mining (Nasdaq: SSRM) completed its previously announced acquisition of Roxmore Resources and signaled that the adjacent Converse gold project in Nevada is a likely next acquisition, aiming to consolidate a district-scale position in the state. The strategic expansion news arrived alongside SSR's Q3 results showing AISC tracking 10% above guidance, suggesting management is leaning on asset growth rather than cost compression as the lever to restore market confidence at current gold prices above $4,000.

headline: VICTORY BATTERY METALS BETS ON URANIUM — Battery Explorer Pivots Hard Into Nuclear as Equities Trade at Steep Discount
snippet: Victory Battery Metals announced a strategic pivot into uranium exploration, joining a growing list of small-cap companies repositioning toward nuclear fuel as uranium long-term contract prices hold at record levels while junior equities trade at multi-year discounts. The move reflects a widening consensus among junior management teams that uranium's structural demand story — driven by accelerating global nuclear construction — now outweighs the near-term headwinds in lithium and graphite markets.

headline: SP ANGEL NOV 5 MARKET VIEW — Copper Physical Tightness, Uranium Disconnect, Post-Midterm Dollar the Day's Three Themes
snippet: SP Angel's Thursday November 5 morning note flags three main themes for mining investors: LME copper's resilience despite futures selling pressure as China physical demand holds firm; the persistent disconnect between uranium long-term contract prices at record levels and equity valuations still near multi-year lows; and the post-midterm US dollar fade as a structural tailwind for dollar-denominated commodities heading into year-end. The London-based mining broker's daily views are closely read by institutional investors with exposure to London-listed and TSX-dual-listed resource names.

headline: 3 CANADIAN NUCLEAR STOCKS FOR NOVEMBER — Cameco Leads Analyst Picks as Sector Trades at Deep Discount to Contract Prices
snippet: Simply Wall St's November 2026 nuclear stocks analysis identifies three Canadian uranium names — led by Cameco (TSX: CCO) — as well-positioned setups ahead of a catalyst-heavy period that includes the November 10 China rare earth export control decision and an approaching wave of Q3 earnings. The analysis highlights the growing disconnect between uranium long-term contract prices at multi-year highs and equity valuations that have not kept pace, mirroring the thesis behind Lobo Tiggre's widely-read Kitco piece earlier this week.
